question: Pentostatin is an inhibitor of the enzyme adenosine deaminase. How is your mechanism of inhibition?

options.opc: It is an analogous inhibitor of the transition state.
options.opd: It is an irreversible covalent inhibitor.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pentostatin" -> "binds to active site" -> "mimics transition state" -> "inhibits adenosine deaminase" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Pentostatin" -> "binds to enzyme" -> "forms covalent bond" -> "irreversible inhibition" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Pentostatin" -> "binds to enzyme" -> "alters enzyme conformation" -> "possible allosteric inhibition" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Pentostatin" -> "binds to enzyme" -> "enzyme attempts catalysis" -> "enzyme inactivation" -> "suicide inhibition" -> 70%
analysis: Pentostatin is known to be a transition state analog inhibitor of adenosine deaminase. It mimics the transition state of the substrate during the enzymatic reaction, thereby inhibiting the enzyme by binding more tightly than the actual substrate. This mechanism is distinct from suicide inhibition, allosteric inhibition, or irreversible covalent inhibition.
